h: Insider tips for your Exeter game
p: Whether you're a puzzle pro or a nervous newbie, a couple of simple habits will help your team. Start by sweeping the room, opening anything that opens and noting anything that looks odd: a number, a symbol, a strange word. Pile up everything you find in one place. Then talk it through together. Nine times out of ten, the clue to a lock is somewhere in that pile, it just needs the right person to spot the link. And don't be too proud to take a hint when the minutes are slipping away.

Students often make the most of escape rooms in Exeter, and it's easy to see why. It's a social activity that works for a group of mixed personalities, there's no physical skill involved, and everybody gets a moment to shine. Families with older children love it too, especially when the kids beat the grown-ups to the answer.

After your game, there's loads to explore close by. The Royal Albert Memorial Museum, known locally as RAMM, is a short walk away on Queen Street and is free to visit, with collections ranging from natural history to world cultures. Next door, Rougemont Gardens sit beside the remains of the old castle and are a peaceful spot for a sit-down. For something truly different, Exeter's Underground Passages, the medieval tunnels that once carried water beneath the city, offer guided tours that are a big hit with curious kids. Princesshay is right by the Guildhall Centre for more shopping and food, and if the sun's out, a trip out to Topsham along the Exe estuary makes for a lovely afternoon.
